title: Clinical Pace Table: Daily Fingerstick Testing by Treatment and Regimen
content:
When the test strips a Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program customer has used are counted, the strips counted for a day of use are set by the customer's treatment class on the testing supplies program and by the insulin regimen recorded on the customer's open Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

**Table rule.** In place of 1.5 strips, the strips counted for a day of use are 5.0 strips for an insulin-treated customer whose open CGM program records the insulin regimen insulin pump, 4.0 strips for an insulin-treated customer whose open CGM program records multiple daily injections or who holds no open CGM program, and 1.5 strips for any other customer. An open CGM program is one that is not closed — referral received, pending authorization, active or on hold.

| Treatment class on the testing supplies program | Open CGM program and its recorded regimen | Strips counted for a day of use |
|---|---|---|
| insulin-treated | open, insulin pump | 5.0 |
| insulin-treated | open, multiple daily injections | 4.0 |
| insulin-treated | no open CGM program (none held, or only closed ones) | 4.0 |
| insulin-treated | open, any other regimen (basal insulin only, or a non-insulin regimen) | 1.5 |
| not treated with insulin | any | 1.5 |

**Sources of the facts.** The treatment class is the one documented on the written order and recorded on the testing supplies program; the regimen is the one recorded on the CGM program.

**Example (hypothetical).** Over 40 days of use, an insulin-treated customer whose CGM program is on hold with the regimen insulin pump is counted at 5.0 strips a day, that is 200 strips.
